## Metadata QC
```{r}
metadata |>
  summarise(
    n_samples = n(),
    n_participants = n_distinct(participant_id),
    missing_sample_ids = sum(is.na(sample_id)),
    duplicate_sample_ids = sum(duplicated(sample_id)),
    missing_participant_ids = sum(is.na(participant_id)),
    duplicate_participant_ids = sum(duplicated(participant_id))
  )
```

Check missing values in each metadata column:

```{r}
metadata |>
  summarise(across(everything(), ~ sum(is.na(.x)))) |>
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "column", values_to = "missing_values")
```

```{r}
datasets <- list(
  metadata = metadata,
  species = microbiome_counts,
  taxonomy = microbiome_taxonomy,
  genes = rnaseq_counts,
  genes_2_annot = gene_annotation,
  cytokine_df = cytokines
)

qc_data <- purrr::imap_dfr(datasets, function(data, dataset_name) {
  tibble::tibble(
    dataset = dataset_name,
    rows = nrow(data),
    columns = ncol(data),
    missing_cells = sum(is.na(data)),
    rows_with_missing = sum(!complete.cases(data)),
    duplicate_rows = sum(duplicated(data))
  )
})

qc_table <- qc_data %>%
  gtsummary::tbl_summary(
    by = dataset,
    include = c(rows, columns, missing_cells, rows_with_missing, duplicate_rows),
    statistic = gtsummary::all_continuous() ~ "{mean}",
    digits = gtsummary::all_continuous() ~ 0,
    label = list(
      rows ~ "Rows",
      columns ~ "Columns",
      missing_cells ~ "Missing cells",
      rows_with_missing ~ "Rows with missing values",
      duplicate_rows ~ "Duplicate rows"
    ),
    missing = "no"
  )

qc_table  # Display the table in the rendered report

gt::gtsave(
  gtsummary::as_gt(qc_table),
  filename = here::here("group_project", "qc_table.html")
)
```


###Do the three methods differ in community composition?


```{r}
run_arm_permanova <- function(distance_name, transform_name) {
  result <- ps_species |>
    tax_transform(transform_name, rank = "species") |>
    dist_calc(distance_name) |>
    dist_permanova(variables = "arm", n_perms = 999, seed = 1) |>
    perm_get() |>
    as.data.frame()

  tibble::tibble(
    distance = distance_name,
    R2 = result["arm", "R2"],
    F = result["arm", "F"],
    p_value = result["arm", "Pr(>F)"]
  )
}
permanova_results <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  run_arm_permanova("bray", "identity"),
  run_arm_permanova("jaccard", "binary"),
  run_arm_permanova("aitchison", "identity")
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    distance = factor(
      distance,
      levels = c("bray", "jaccard", "aitchison"),
      labels = c("Bray-Curtis", "Jaccard", "Aitchison")
    )
  )
permanova_table_data <- permanova_results |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    p_value = dplyr::if_else(
      p_value < 0.001,
      "<0.001",
      sprintf("%.3f", p_value)
    )
  ) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    Test = distance,
    `R-squared (R²)` = R2,
    `F statistic` = F,
    `P-value` = p_value
  )
permanova_gt <- gt::gt(permanova_table_data) |>
  gt::tab_header(
    title = gt::md("PERMANOVA: Community composition by contraceptive arm"),
    subtitle = "Tests compare injectable, pill, and ring groups (999 permutations)"
  ) |>
  gt::fmt_number(columns = `R-squared (R²)`, decimals = 3) |>
  gt::fmt_number(columns = `F statistic`, decimals = 2) |>
  gt::cols_label(Test = "Distance metric") |>
  gt::cols_align(align = "center", columns = -Test) |>
  gt::tab_options(
    table.width = gt::pct(100),
    table.font.size = gt::px(14),
    heading.title.font.size = gt::px(16),
    data_row.padding = gt::px(6),
    row.striping.include_table_body = TRUE
  ) |>
  gt::tab_source_note(
    source_note = gt::md(
      "R² is the proportion of community variation associated with contraceptive arm. P-values below 0.001 are shown as <0.001."
    )
  )

permanova_gt
table_dir <- here::here("group_project", "tables")
dir.create(table_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

gt::gtsave(
  permanova_gt,
  filename = file.path(table_dir, "community_permanova_group_2.html")
)
```


### Is bacterial vaginosis more common in one arm?

```{r}
bv_arm_levels <- c("injectable", "pill", "ring")
bv_categories <- c("negative", "intermediate", "positive")

if (!all(c("arm", "bv") %in% names(metadata))) {
  stop("metadata must contain arm and bv columns.")
}
if (anyNA(metadata$arm) || anyNA(metadata$bv)) {
  stop("Missing arm or BV values must be resolved before this comparison.")
}
if (!all(metadata$arm %in% bv_arm_levels)) {
  stop("Unexpected arm values found in metadata.")
}
if (!all(metadata$bv %in% bv_categories)) {
  stop("Unexpected BV categories found; check metadata$bv.")
}

bv_data <- metadata %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    arm = factor(arm, levels = bv_arm_levels),
    bv = factor(bv, levels = bv_categories),
    bv_status = factor(
      ifelse(bv == "positive", "Positive", "Not positive"),
      levels = c("Not positive", "Positive")
    )
  )


bv_categories_table <- gtsummary::tbl_cross(
  data = bv_data,
  row = bv,
  col = arm,
  percent = "column",
  margin = "column",
  digits = 1,
  label = list(bv ~ "BV category", arm ~ "Contraceptive arm")
) %>%
  gtsummary::modify_caption(
    "BV categories by contraceptive arm"
  ) %>%
  gtsummary::bold_labels()


bv_prevalence_table <- gtsummary::tbl_cross(
  data = bv_data,
  row = bv_status,
  col = arm,
  percent = "column",
  margin = "column",
  digits = 1,
  label = list(bv_status ~ "BV status", arm ~ "Contraceptive arm")
) %>%
  gtsummary::add_p(test = "fisher.test") %>%
  gtsummary::modify_caption(
    "Positive BV prevalence by contraceptive arm"
  ) %>%
  gtsummary::modify_footnote(
    gtsummary::all_stat_cols() ~
      "Values are participant counts and percentages within arm. Fisher's exact test compares positive with not positive BV."
  ) %>%
  gtsummary::bold_labels()

bv_categories_table
bv_prevalence_table


bv_table_dir <- here::here("group_project", "tables")
dir.create(bv_table_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

gt::gtsave(
  gtsummary::as_gt(bv_categories_table),
  filename = file.path(bv_table_dir, "bv_categories_by_arm_group_2.html")
)
gt::gtsave(
  gtsummary::as_gt(bv_prevalence_table),
  filename = file.path(bv_table_dir, "bv_prevalence_by_arm_group_2.html")
)
```
##BV presence was not significantly different between arms (Fisher's exact test p = 0.6).


##The ring is delivered locally and the other two are systemic. Does the ring differ from the other two in host gene expression?



```{r}

library(DESeq2)

# Make the comparison group from the metadata, not from the gene counts
meta <- as.data.frame(metadata)

if (anyNA(meta$arm) || anyNA(meta$rnaseq_batch)) {
  stop("Resolve missing arm or rnaseq_batch values before analysis.")
}

meta$delivery <- factor(
  ifelse(meta$arm == "ring", "ring", "systemic"),
  levels = c("systemic", "ring")
)
meta$rnaseq_batch <- factor(meta$rnaseq_batch)

# The first column contains gene IDs; the remaining columns are raw counts
count_df <- as.data.frame(rnaseq_counts)
gene_ids <- count_df[[1]]
count_mat <- as.matrix(count_df[-1])
rownames(count_mat) <- gene_ids

if (anyDuplicated(gene_ids)) {
  stop("Gene IDs are duplicated in the RNA-seq count table.")
}
if (any(!is.finite(count_mat)) || any(count_mat < 0) ||
    any(count_mat != floor(count_mat))) {
  stop("RNA-seq values must be non-negative whole-number raw counts.")
}
storage.mode(count_mat) <- "integer"

# Match metadata rows to the count-table sample columns
if (anyDuplicated(meta$sample_id) ||
    !setequal(colnames(count_mat), meta$sample_id)) {
  stop("RNA-seq sample IDs and metadata sample IDs do not match.")
}

meta <- meta[match(colnames(count_mat), meta$sample_id), ]
rownames(meta) <- meta$sample_id
stopifnot(identical(colnames(count_mat), rownames(meta)))

# Check that delivery group and sequencing batch are not completely confounded
design_matrix <- model.matrix(~ rnaseq_batch + delivery, data = meta)
if (qr(design_matrix)$rank < ncol(design_matrix)) {
  stop("Batch and delivery group are confounded; this model cannot separate their effects.")
}

# Remove genes with very low total counts, then run the differential-expression test
keep <- rowSums(count_mat) >= 10
dds <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(
  countData = count_mat[keep, ],
  colData = meta,
  design = ~ rnaseq_batch + delivery
)

dds <- DESeq(dds)

# Positive log2FoldChange means higher expression in ring users
res <- results(
  dds,
  contrast = c("delivery", "ring", "systemic"),
  alpha = 0.05
)

results_table <- as.data.frame(res) |>
  tibble::rownames_to_column("gene_id") |>
  dplyr::arrange(padj)

# Show the 20 genes with the smallest adjusted p-values
results_table |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(padj)) |>
  dplyr::slice_head(n = 20)

# Count genes meeting the chosen false-discovery threshold
sum(results_table$padj < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE)
```

Replace `test = "fisher.test"` with `test = "chisq.test"`:

```r
bv_prevalence_table <- gtsummary::tbl_cross(
  data = bv_data,
  row = bv_status,
  col = arm,
  percent = "column",
  margin = "column",
  digits = 1,
  label = list(bv_status ~ "BV status", arm ~ "Contraceptive arm")
) %>%
  gtsummary::add_p(test = "chisq.test") %>%
  gtsummary::modify_caption(
    "Positive BV prevalence by contraceptive arm"
  ) %>%
  gtsummary::modify_footnote(
    gtsummary::all_stat_cols() ~
      "Values are participant counts and percentages within arm. Pearson's chi-square test compares positive with not positive BV."
  ) %>%
  gtsummary::bold_labels()
```

The chi-square test checks whether BV status and contraceptive arm are associated. It relies on expected counts being sufficiently large; if several expected cell counts are small, its p-value may be unreliable. You can inspect the expected counts with:

```r
chisq.test(table(bv_data$bv_status, bv_data$arm))$expected
```

As a common rule of thumb, expected counts should generally be at least 5.

Copilot: Yes—here is R code to compare **ring users with injectable and pill users combined**, using the raw RNA-seq counts already loaded in your document. It adjusts for `rnaseq_batch` and checks that the samples line up before testing.

Add this as an R chunk after loading `metadata` and `rnaseq_counts`:

```r
library(DESeq2)

# Make the comparison group from the metadata, not from the gene counts
meta <- as.data.frame(metadata)

if (anyNA(meta$arm) || anyNA(meta$rnaseq_batch)) {
  stop("Resolve missing arm or rnaseq_batch values before analysis.")
}

meta$delivery <- factor(
  ifelse(meta$arm == "ring", "ring", "systemic"),
  levels = c("systemic", "ring")
)
meta$rnaseq_batch <- factor(meta$rnaseq_batch)

# The first column contains gene IDs; the remaining columns are raw counts
count_df <- as.data.frame(rnaseq_counts)
gene_ids <- count_df[[1]]
count_mat <- as.matrix(count_df[-1])
rownames(count_mat) <- gene_ids

if (anyDuplicated(gene_ids)) {
  stop("Gene IDs are duplicated in the RNA-seq count table.")
}
if (any(!is.finite(count_mat)) || any(count_mat < 0) ||
    any(count_mat != floor(count_mat))) {
  stop("RNA-seq values must be non-negative whole-number raw counts.")
}
storage.mode(count_mat) <- "integer"

# Match metadata rows to the count-table sample columns
if (anyDuplicated(meta$sample_id) ||
    !setequal(colnames(count_mat), meta$sample_id)) {
  stop("RNA-seq sample IDs and metadata sample IDs do not match.")
}

meta <- meta[match(colnames(count_mat), meta$sample_id), ]
rownames(meta) <- meta$sample_id
stopifnot(identical(colnames(count_mat), rownames(meta)))

# Check that delivery group and sequencing batch are not completely confounded
design_matrix <- model.matrix(~ rnaseq_batch + delivery, data = meta)
if (qr(design_matrix)$rank < ncol(design_matrix)) {
  stop("Batch and delivery group are confounded; this model cannot separate their effects.")
}

# Remove genes with very low total counts, then run the differential-expression test
keep <- rowSums(count_mat) >= 10
dds <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(
  countData = count_mat[keep, ],
  colData = meta,
  design = ~ rnaseq_batch + delivery
)

dds <- DESeq(dds)

# Positive log2FoldChange means higher expression in ring users
res <- results(
  dds,
  contrast = c("delivery", "ring", "systemic"),
  alpha = 0.05
)

results_table <- as.data.frame(res) |>
  tibble::rownames_to_column("gene_id") |>
  dplyr::arrange(padj)

# Show the 20 genes with the smallest adjusted p-values
results_table |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(padj)) |>
  dplyr::slice_head(n = 20)

# Count genes meeting the chosen false-discovery threshold
sum(results_table$padj < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE)
```

**Result:** `log2FoldChange` compares ring to systemic users; positive values mean higher expression in the ring group, negative values mean lower. `padj` is the multiple-testing-adjusted p-value, which helps account for testing many genes. The final line counts genes with `padj < 0.05`.

This tests for an **association** between delivery group and gene expression, not proof that delivery method caused a difference. The batch check matters because if the ring and systemic samples are separated entirely by sequencing batch, the data cannot distinguish a batch effect from a delivery-group effect.
